cands.bio: Republican member of the Alabama State Senate for District 16 since 1990. He served in the Alabama House of Representatives from 1966 to 1983. He was Senate minority leader 2002-2010 and majority leader 2011-2014. He holds a law degree and is president of Birmingham Business Consultants LLC.
cands.gaps: We could not find where he was born or raised, or when he came to Alabama. We found no stated positions from him on data centers, homestead taxes, land ownership, growth, immigration, guns, abortion, schools or policing. We found no details of the bills he has sponsored; the source's sponsored-bill list was empty. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2022 or 2026. We found no endorsements for the 2026 race and no documented controversies or foreign ties.

cands.name: Spencer Stone

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Computer science teacher and coach, formerly an English and History teacher. Has a Ph.D. from the University of Alabama (2015). Ballotpedia also lists him as a business owner. Democratic nominee for Alabama State Senate District 16 in 2026. Has not held elected office.

endorsements.text: Alabama Democratic County Chairs' Association (2026), per his campaign site
Alabama AFL-CIO (2026), per his campaign site
Alabama New South Coalition (2026), per his campaign site
Listed by Ballotpedia as recommended in the voter guides 'Reject AIPAC from City Council to Congress' (Vote for Peace), 'Tabitha's List' and 'Unburdening The Ballot'
Campaign site says he received the 2026 Moms Demand Action Gun Sense Candidate distinction, and notes it is not an endorsement from Moms Demand Action or Everytown

cands.gaps: We could not find where or when Stone was born, or whether and when he moved to Alabama; his upbringing is inferred from his Pelham High School diploma and his campaign's wording. We found no details on the business he owns, how long he has taught, or his Montevallo degrees. He has held no elected office, so there are no legislative actions to report. We found no stated positions from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, immigration or H-1B, policing, abortion, or vouchers and school choice. We found no controversies, foreign ties, or land-use statements about data centers or development beyond his general campaign language.

local.label: Roots 90: Ballotpedia says he graduated from Pelham High School, and his campaign site calls District 16 the community that raised him and says he and his wife chose to raise their family there; his birthplace is not stated.

score.why: Raised $2,362, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: High school teacher (computer science, earlier English and History) and coach; Ballotpedia lists career experience as educator and business owner. He has a Ph.D. from the University of Alabama and graduate degrees from the University of Montevallo. No elected office or legislative or budget work is documented.
qual.why: He has no prior legislative service, and teaching is not directly related to writing law and budgets. The business-owner background is noted but no details were found, so he scores in the low-to-middle range.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Says on his campaign site that he wants competitive teacher pay that keeps educators in Alabama. The page names no raise percentage and says nothing about vouchers, charters or school choice.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Says on his campaign site that Alabama can grow industry "without wrecking our land and water" and calls for responsible development that protects property values and natural resources, with growth and conservation in balance.
